step_goal: Compile a syntax-safe HearthRanger VisionAI `GlobalValues.json` by copying the active runtime default baseline, preserving the documented board-value model, profiling every copied key, and limiting pre-run deck-specific changes to explicitly authorized overlays instead of speculative broad tuning.
required_inputs: The official HearthRanger `GlobalValues` help page and the generic VisionAI JSON-config page so the compiler uses documented file shape, board-value semantics, and turn-weight semantics.
Access to the active runtime baseline file `CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json`, because the official page strongly recommends copying that file before editing.
A validated `global_values_contract` or equivalent gameplan section that states whether pre-run overlays are forbidden or allowed, which keys are allowed, and why.
A baseline hash and runtime surface snapshot for the exact default `GlobalValues.json` that was copied.
A full-key profile step that classifies every copied baseline key before deck-local output is written.
If any overlay is requested, an explicit `old_value`, new `value`, rationale, rollback note, and source references for each changed key.
produced_outputs: A deck-local `CustomConfig/<deck>/GlobalValues.json` that preserves the copied baseline shape and keeps `GameCardId` equal to `GlobalValues`.
A `global_values_key_profile_report.json` artifact that records every baseline key, its classification, whether it stayed baseline or received a pre-run overlay, and any blocking reasons.
Row-level provenance entries for each emitted `values` row so every preserved or overlaid row can be traced back to a contract clause and source.
A preview receipt or equivalent report that records baseline source path, baseline hash, overlay keys, and validation status.
A machine-readable board-value contract that links documented board-value components to local downstream review expectations.
reliable_uses: Create a strict-JSON `GlobalValues.json` that uses the documented object-plus-`values`-array shape instead of legacy scalar entries.
Preserve the documented board-value formula: own hand, hero, hero power, weapon, secret, minions, and deck minus the corresponding opponent components.
Preserve the documented final-board-value formula by emitting `FirstTurnValueWeight` and `SecondTurnValueWeight` as normal `values` blocks.
Copy every key that exists in the active runtime default baseline instead of inventing a reduced custom file shape.
Profile copied keys into categories such as turn-weight review candidates, own-side board-value surfaces, opponent-side board-value surfaces, or baseline-preserved keys.
Apply narrow pre-run overlays to documented turn-weight keys when a gameplan explicitly authorizes them, the baseline `old_value` matches, and the change stays deck-local.
Keep broad minion, hero, weapon, secret, and deck-related value families at their copied baseline when no source-backed authorization exists.
limitations: This step can preserve documented syntax and documented board-value semantics, but it cannot prove that a changed `GlobalValues.json` improves gameplay or even that HearthRanger loaded it correctly in a fresh runtime session.

The official `GlobalValues` page documents the board-value formula, `FirstTurnValueWeight`, `SecondTurnValueWeight`, and an example such as `GlobalDivineShield`, but it does not publish a complete machine-readable public catalog for every live runtime key.

This step must not infer that an aggressive archetype automatically justifies broad edits to hero, minion, weapon, secret, or deck-related values; the public docs only clearly document the turn-weight surface as a direct board-value policy control.

Changing many `GlobalValues` keys at once is high risk because a deck-wide global change can affect many unrelated decisions; this compiler architecture should therefore avoid broad pre-run tuning batches.

[uncertain] The public docs and cached registry do not prove that every live `GlobalValues` key name and meaning will stay version-stable across future HearthRanger releases, so HSConfig should treat the active runtime baseline as authoritative and diffable rather than hard-coding a frozen key list.
relevant_config_surfaces: `CustomConfig/deck_config.ini` `[CONFIGS]` mapping from exact deck name to config directory.
`CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json` as the authoritative runtime baseline source to copy.
The upstream `global_values_contract` or equivalent gameplan section that authorizes baseline-only behavior or narrow overlays.
The local board-value contract surface used for later review, such as `board_value_model` and `board_value_components`.
aggressive_generation_policy: Be aggressive about preserving the full runtime default baseline, not aggressive about inventing new numeric values. A complete copied baseline is safer than a short custom file.

Use archetype-specific aggression first through the documented turn-weight surface, because the public docs explicitly describe first-turn versus second-turn weighting and give an aggro-style example.
Apply pre-run overlays only to an explicitly allowed narrow key set, and require `old_value` matching against the copied baseline before any row is changed.
Keep non-turn-weight keys such as minion, hero, weapon, secret, and deck-related value groups at their copied baseline unless a later evidence-backed workflow authorizes a narrower change.
Prefer a small deck-local overlay on top of the copied baseline over emitting a reduced file that contains only the changed keys.

Do not translate vague guide claims such as `play more aggressively`, `value face more`, or `protect board better` into unsupported broad `GlobalValues` edits; keep those claims in contracts or reports until a concrete documented key mapping exists.
If an archetype-specific profile is emitted pre-run, make it reversible, hash-bound to the copied baseline, and clearly labeled as a preview assumption rather than a proven optimal policy.
validation_gates: The research result must cover every required field from `fields.yaml` and pass `validate_json.py` for this research batch.
Generated `GlobalValues.json` must be strict JSON with no comments or trailing commas.
The emitted file must be based on a copied baseline whose hash and source path are recorded in the receipt or profile report.
At minimum, `FirstTurnValueWeight` and `SecondTurnValueWeight` must exist and each must be an object containing a `values` array with `condition` and `value` fields.
Every baseline key copied from `CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json` must appear in the key profile report, and the profiled key count must match the loaded baseline key count.
Any overlay key must already exist in the baseline, and its declared `old_value` must match the copied baseline value before the overlay is accepted.
Every emitted row must have provenance linking it to either baseline materialization or an explicitly authorized overlay rule.
Any requested non-turn-weight change without fresh supporting evidence must fail closed or remain report-only instead of being emitted.
architectural_implications: HSConfig should implement a dedicated `GlobalValues` compiler pipeline rather than treating the file as free-form JSON text.
That pipeline should be staged as baseline load -> baseline shape validation -> all-key profile -> optional overlay authorization -> deck-local file emission -> receipt and provenance generation.
The baseline loader should read `CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json` from the active runtime root and deep-copy the document before any edits are considered.

The syntax model should distinguish a narrow guaranteed minimum key set from the broader live baseline inventory, because the active runtime may contain more keys than the public minimum example shows.
A `global_values_contract` should be mandatory whenever overlays are allowed, with explicit `patch_authorization`, `baseline_hash_required`, `required_evidence`, and per-overlay metadata.

Step 1 pre-run overlays and Step 2 evidence-backed tuning must remain separate lanes. Step 1 may authorize only narrow documented assumptions, while later tuning must require fresh legal-option and outcome evidence.

Local board-value review should use a component contract that maps own and opponent hero, weapon, and minion families to candidate `GlobalValues` keys while keeping unsupported components as formula-only or evidence-required surfaces.
Deck-local `GlobalValues` patches should never mutate `CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json`; the default file is the source baseline, not the patch target.
recommended_contracts: A `pre_run_assumption_overlays` structure for authorized Step 1 overlays, where each row contains `key`, `old_value`, `value`, `reason`, `expected_effect`, `risk`, `rollback`, and `source_refs`.
A `global_values_key_profile_report.json` contract with baseline counts, classifications, blocking reasons, overlay keys, and per-key actions.
A `config_row_provenance.json` or equivalent receipt section that records file path, JSON pointer, source doc key, source gameplan key, confidence, and patchability for each emitted row.
A shared `board_value_model` contract that preserves the documented board-value formula and its Step 1 boundary.

A `global_values_key_authority.json` matrix for later review work that records which key families may ever be considered for evidence-backed tuning and the minimum repeat or review posture they require.
A runtime surface snapshot contract that captures the current default `GlobalValues.json` hash and other config lineage needed before later deck-local tuning.
never_autogenerate_without: The official HearthRanger `GlobalValues` help page and generic JSON-config page cited in the compilation receipt or manifest.
Access to the active runtime baseline `CustomConfig/default/GlobalValues.json`, or a clearly labeled fallback path that is not mistaken for a full live baseline.
Successful baseline shape validation proving that the copied file uses `values` blocks and includes required turn-weight keys.
A baseline hash and runtime surface snapshot for the copied default file.
An explicit contract that says whether overlays are forbidden or allowed before fresh runtime evidence exists.
For any overlay, a documented key mapping, baseline `old_value` match, rollback note, and source-backed rationale.
For any non-turn-weight change, fresh runtime evidence tied to the current deck, active config hash, legal options, chosen actions, and outcomes.
A passing provenance and profile pass showing that every copied baseline key was considered.
